parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes to overhaul the private rented sector by abolishing no-fault evictions, preventing landlords from exploiting renters, empowering tenants to challenge unreasonable rent increases, and extending building safety standards including Awaab's Law to the private sector.

citations.quote: We will end Section 21 'no fault' evictions, prevent private renters being exploited and discriminated against,
empower them to challenge unreasonable rent increases, and take steps to decisively raise standards, including extending `Awaab's Law' to the private sector.

results.headline: Labour pledges 1.5 million new homes next parliament
results.quote: Labour will get Britain building again, creating jobs across England, with 1.5 million new homes over the next parliament.

results.headline: Starmer hails biggest renters' rights upgrade in a generation
results.quote: I am very proud — this Government are very proud — of the biggest upgrade in workers' rights in a generation and the biggest upgrade in renters' rights in a generation and of doing the most any Government have ever done to reduce child poverty.

results.headline: Starmer: upgrading renters' rights and building 1.5 million homes
results.quote: We are going to build 1.5 million homes. We are upgrading the rights of renters, because we know how important it is for everyone to have a safe and secure roof over their head.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives propose passing a Renters Reform Bill to deliver fairness for landlords and renters, including delivering court reforms necessary to fully abolish Section 21, and strengthening grounds for possession against anti-social behaviour by tenants.

citations.quote: We will pass a Renters Reform Bill that will deliver fairness in the rental market for landlords and renters alike. We will deliver the court reforms necessary to fully abolish Section 21 and strengthen other grounds for landlords behaviour.
introduce a two-year temporary Capital Gains Tax relief for landlords who sell to their existing tenants.

results.headline: Conservatives pledge 1.6 million new homes in England
results.quote: We will deliver 1.6 million homes in England in the next Parliament.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, creating a national register of licensed landlords, and introducing proactive enforcement of clear standards for socially rented homes including strict time limits for repairs.

citations.quote: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords.
Proactively enforcing clear standards for homes that are socially rented, including strict time limits for repairs.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge to ban no-fault evictions immediately
results.quote: Delivering a fair deal for renters by immediately banning no-fault evictions, making three-year tenancies the default, and creating a national register of licensed landlords.

parties.name: Plaid Cymru
parties.summary: Plaid Cymru advocates for a system of fair rents and rent controls in the private rental sector to ensure affordability for local people, proposing a Right to Adequate Housing Bill in Wales that would include powers to introduce rent controls and other market interventions.

citations.quote: Within the private rental sector, we believe in a system of fair rents and rent control so that they are affordable to local people on local incomes, and that individuals and families are not priced out of the area where they currently live.
Our proposed Right to Adequate Housing Bill in Wales would include powers to introduce rent controls and other market interventions to make housing more affordable.

results.headline: Plaid Cymru: right to a safe and affordable home, with rent controls
results.quote: Plaid Cymru believes that everybody has the right to a safe and affordable home in their community, and this should be the purpose of the housing system. We will introduce a Right to Adequate Housing which will underpin this.
